ENT Clinical Note

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure:
  • Main concern today is 3-day history of watery diarrhoea with mild abdominal pain and one episode of vomiting. No identified food, medication, or environmental trigger for an ENT‐type reaction.
- Symptom timeline and progression:
  • Onset sudden 3 days ago; neither improving nor worsening.
- ENT symptoms:
  • Throat swelling/closure sensation: Denied.
  • Voice change/hoarseness: Denied.
  • Dysphagia/odynophagia, drooling: Denied.
  • Nasal/ocular symptoms: Not reported.
  • Stridor/noisy breathing, dyspnoea: Baseline mild asthma only; no new/worsening dyspnoea.
  • Facial/lip/tongue/uvular swelling: Denied.
  • Ear pain/hearing changes: Not reported.
  • Neck pain/swelling: Denied.
- Relevant past episodes and treatments:
  • No prior similar ENT or allergic reactions reported.
  • No previous ED visits or epinephrine use for allergy.
- Allergies and current medications:
  • Allergies: NKDA stated.
  • Medications: Asthma inhaler (brand recently changed; dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Social context:
  • Currently at home; no mention of accompaniment.

Objective:
- Observable swelling: None reported.
- Airway/breathing: No stridor, no increased work of breathing.
- Mental status: Alert, conversational.
- Vitals and physical exam findings: Not recorded.
- Presence of another person: Not stated.

Assessment:
- Working clinical impression: No evidence of upper-airway or ENT allergic reaction; gastrointestinal illness (likely viral gastroenteritis) is the primary issue.
  Evidence: Acute watery diarrhoea, brief vomiting, no ENT swelling, no respiratory compromise.
- DDx items aligning with transcript (from system output):
  1. Acute infectious (viral) gastroenteritis – High likelihood: sudden watery diarrhoea, mild abdominal cramps, self-limited vomiting, no blood/fever.
  2. Bacterial food-borne gastroenteritis – Medium likelihood: similar symptom cluster, though lack of fever/blood makes this less likely.
  3. Irritable bowel syndrome/post-infectious functional diarrhoea – Low-medium likelihood: pain relieved by defecation and baseline anxiety, but very acute onset opposes.
- No ENT-specific differential needed; no conflict noted between transcript and DDx.

Plan:
- Immediate actions/advice:
  • Encourage adequate oral rehydration (water, oral rehydration salts if available).
  • Monitor for fever, persistent vomiting, bloody stool, or signs of dehydration.
- Patient instructions:
  • Remain at home, rest, and maintain hydration.
  • Seek urgent in-person care (GP or emergency department) if abdominal pain worsens, develops high fever, blood in stool/vomit, or inability to keep fluids down.
  • No specific allergen avoidance or epinephrine requirement at this time due to absence of allergic features.
- Follow-up:
  • Re-evaluate in 24–48 hours with primary care provider if no improvement.
  • Longer-term: discuss colorectal cancer screening with GP given family history (non-ENT).
  • Asthma inhaler review with GP to ensure correct usage and adequate supply.

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing but expected elements for acute ENT/allergy presentation: vital signs, formal airway examination, documentation of uvular/tongue inspection, confirmation of auto-injector availability, comprehensive drug/allergy list.
● Conflicts between transcript and DDx: None.
● Transcript quality: Clear audio; occasional minor interruptions but clinically adequate.
